headline: The head of the International Monetary Fund warned that AI is already reducing demand for many workers and could strain the taxes governments collect on work.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: the Bloomberg text matches the headline and the warning is hers, though it is a call to act and gives no figures for job or tax losses.
importance_line: The head of the IMF says AI's effect on jobs and on the tax base is already visible, which bears first on young and entry-level workers, then on governments that depend on taxes from work, then on companies; the report gives no figures for job or tax losses, and her growth estimate covers only advanced Asian economies.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by The Japan Times, that Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the lender that advises governments on their economies, told the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Monday 12 Oct that AI is "a slow-moving tsunami" which is already hollowing out demand for many workers by taking over routine tasks, while adding low-paying jobs in sectors such as construction, "not a story to celebrate", and which risks straining government revenue because it shifts the economy's weight toward capital and away from labour, the traditional source of tax income. She urged policymakers to rethink education and act now, while noting the IMF's estimate that AI could lift growth in advanced Asian economies by as much as one percentage point, a boost she said would "more than offset" the drag from ageing; it follows her 7 Oct 2026 Singapore speech urging faster action on debt, which our 8 Oct 2026 edition carried from the Associated Press.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); read Bloomberg's text on The Japan Times (credited Bloomberg), url kept as Bloomberg's own link. What is new today: the 'tsunami' warning on jobs and tax revenue at the Bangkok meetings; the 8 Oct item was a different speech on debt.
